cause: PORT FWD crane went down, halting handling operations during 30" conductor running/cementing prep.
remedy: Waited for crane to be restored before resuming.
free_text: "Halted operations due to PORT FWD crane down." Depth is the day's end/header depth (258 m, hole TD reached earlier same day); no explicit line depth given for the crane outage itself.

cause: Burst disk on top-up pipe ruptured during a pressure/circulation test (53 bar/189 L); cement unit then alarmed on overpressure and the Halliburton control screen froze, unable to sign out alarms.
remedy: Manually operated cement unit to step up rate and confirm open flow path; performed a remedial cement job (10 m3 1.56 SG G-cement slurry via cement hose/top-up pipe, displaced with 1.1 m3 SW).
free_text: "Pressured up to 53 bar / 189 l, burst disk at 14 m below ML / 159 m MD ruptured" ... "Got alarm on overpressured cement unit ... control screen froze up." Explicit line depth 159 m MD used. Classified npt_other (equipment/control-system failure) rather than cementing_issue because the root problem is the burst disk + Halliburton unit lock-up, not a defect in the cement job itself; the remedial cement job is the fix, not the failure.

cause: Forward PRS (pipe racking system) malfunctioned while racking back BHA; fault traced to a proximity switch.
remedy: Trouble-shot and found failure on proximity switch; operations continued.
free_text: "Malfunction of forward PRS. Trouble-shooted same and found failure on proximity switch." No explicit halt duration or NPT stated (ops continued right after) -- kept at low confidence as a borderline call; a specific fault WAS identified, which is why it was kept in rather than dropped like the terser 06-14/07-03/07-12/07-14 PRS/software one-liners with no identified fault.

cause: Raw water pump failed, leaving only 1 of 3 pumps available; drilling operation postponed because this pump also supplies firewater/cooling water.
remedy: Boat brought a replacement pump; troubleshooting and replacement spanned 06-22 to 06-24 before drilling resumed on 06-25.
free_text: "Raw water pumpe failed and left rig with only 1 out of 3 pumpes available ... the drilling operation is postphoned until the pump is replaced." No well depth is relevant (surface utility failure); depth left null rather than forcing the header value. This is the initiating document (06-22); the continuing 'waiting on raw water pump repair' lines in the 06-23 and 06-24 reports are treated as narration of the SAME event, not new events (see HAND_LABELS.md).

cause: Riser leak: picked up off bottom and circulated to investigate; located leak in the wellhead connector, 70-80 l/hr.
remedy: Flow-checked well on trip tank while waiting on a decision; leakage stopped on its own and well flow-checked ok.
free_text: "PU off bottom and circulated due to riser leak. Pumped out to shoe from 296 m to 251 m ... Located leak to be in wellhead connector, 70-80 l/hr." Depth = 296 m, the point drilling was interrupted from.

cause: Gain of 1 m3 observed in active pit while drilling 467-473 m.
remedy: Picked up off bottom and flow-checked well; static after 15 min, resumed drilling.
free_text: "Observed gain of 1 m3 in active. PU off btm and flow checked well static for 15 min. Ok." Canonical terse-shorthand kick pattern (matches extract_events.py SYSTEM_PROMPT Example 3).

cause: Minor fluid loss while flow-checking after reaching 618 m: total loss 140 l over 1.5 hr.
free_text: "MU TDS, rotated 10 rpm and flow checked well. Total loss 140 l over 1.5 hr." Depth = 618 m, the bit depth reached just before this flow check (report also separately states POOH started from 578 m the next paragraph -- kept 618 m as the more directly-tied depth). Minor/ambiguous whether this is a true formation loss or the same wellhead-connector leak being tracked elsewhere; kept as mud_loss at reduced confidence per the round-1/2 audit precedent in VOLVE_EVAL_NOTES.md.

cause: Losses of 3 m3/15 min observed at 655 m while drilling 618-685 m.
remedy: Circulated with reduced flow (1800 lpm); increased flow back to 2250 lpm and still observed continued loss of 200 l/min; total loss for the interval was 10 m3.
free_text: "Observed losses, 3 m3/15 min at 655 m ... Increased flow rate to 2250 lpm and observed loss of 200 l/min. Total loss was 10 m3." Treated as ONE mud_loss episode (not two) since it is a single continuous narrative of losses while drilling one interval.

cause: Escalating leak on the wellhead/riser connector while displacing well to seawater: flow-checked well and observed loss of 500 l/hr, an increasing leak rate versus the 70-170 l/hr background level tracked on earlier days.
free_text: "Flow checked well and observed loss of 500 l/hr. Observed increasing leak rate on connector using seawater." Depth = 890 m (last stated drilling depth before this line, day interval 780-890 m). This is the same wellhead-connector leak first flagged on 06-25 at 70-80 l/hr, now escalated; classified npt_other (a mechanical connector leak to sea, not a formation loss) rather than mud_loss.

cause: Rig ESD (emergency shutdown) system shut down unexpectedly while drilling the 941-1178 m interval.
remedy: Managed to keep rotating string at 10 rpm and pump 200 lpm with the cement unit as a workaround until ESD was restored.
free_text: "Rig ESD system had shut-down. Managed to rotate string 10 rpm and pump 200 lpm with cement unit." No explicit depth on this line; used the day's end depth (1178 m) as the header-implied value.

cause: Rig activity paused: POOH with cement stinger to shoe (251 m) to wait on Siemens software download for the process module, because the ESD systems were by-passed for the work.
remedy: Waited for Siemens software download to complete before continuing.
free_text: "POOH with cement stinger to shoe at 251 m due to upcoming other activity on rig: Waited on Siemens software downloading for process module due to by-passed ESD systems." Explicit line depth 251 m used.

cause: Operation terminated due to Siemens uploading software (process-control/ESD related, continuing from 07-04's software download).
free_text: "Terminated operation due to Siemens uploading of Software." No explicit line depth; used the day's header depth (1353 m, unchanged all day) since the well was not being actively drilled at this point (WOW/rig-up day). Kept as its own event (distinct daily report) from the 07-04 and 07-06 Siemens-related entries per the per-document convention explained in HAND_LABELS.md.

cause: Pulled out of hole to 225 m and stood by, because Siemens software upgrade work took priority on the rig.
free_text: "Pulled out of hole to 225m. Stand-by due to prioity of Siemens to upgrads software." Explicit line depth 225 m used.

cause: Racked back one stand because the ROV failed.
remedy: Circulated at reduced rate while inspecting TDS and continuing ROV repair.
free_text: "Racked back one std due to ROV failure. Meanwhile circ at reduced rate ... Inspected TDS." Depth = 376 m, the drilled depth reached immediately before this line.

cause: One double of 3 1/2" DP came out of the derrick's single latch and leaned over the windwall across the drill floor; operation terminated.
remedy: Investigated the incident while circulating and reciprocating pipe.
free_text: "Terminated operation. Due to one double 3 1/2" DP came out of derrick single latch and leaned over the windwall across the drill floor." ... "Investigated incident with 3 1/2" DP." Serious handling/safety incident, kept separate from the ROV-failure line above (different cause). Depth = 376 m (same drilled depth context).

cause: Tight spot while pulling out of hole with the BHA, F/1348 m T/1330 m.
remedy: Worked string and backreamed (260-440 lpm, 13-37 kNm, 50-70 rpm); max overpull 20 MT.
free_text: "Attempted to POOH w/ BHA, tightspot F/ 1348m T/ 1330m. Worked string/backreamed ... max overpull 20 MT." Canonical tight-spot shorthand pattern (matches extract_events.py SYSTEM_PROMPT Example 3 and the round-1/2 audit's real event at 1348 m).

cause: One mud pump (#3) out of service while circulating hole clean at TD before displacement.
remedy: Restored the following day (07-10: "Mud pump #3 up running").
free_text: "RIH to TD, circulated hole clean with SW ... One mud pump out of services." No explicit halt described (circulating continued at reduced pump capacity); kept as a borderline, low-confidence entry rather than dropped, since it is a genuine equipment-down state. Not duplicated on 07-10 (where the same pump is still down before being restored) -- see HAND_LABELS.md convention.

cause: Running back in hole after tripping, met an obstruction at 1093 m.
remedy: Worked string, lined up tool face high side and pumped through to pass the obstruction at 1093 m; took weight again at 1102 m and repeated the same technique to pass through to 1142 m.
free_text: "Ran back in hole, met obstruction at 1093m, worked string ... passed obstruction at 1093m ... RIH took weight at 1102 m ... passed obstruction. RIH F/1102m T/1142m." Treated as ONE episode (two closely-spaced obstructions on the same RIH run) rather than two separate events; interval 1093-1142 m recorded to capture both.

cause: Overpull of 20 MT while pulling out of hole with the 26" BHA, over two intervals: F/1340 m T/1303 m and F/1102 m T/1002 m.
remedy: Lubricated out through both tight intervals (442 lpm, 2.5 bars, 80 rpm, 8-20 kNm).
free_text: "POOH w/ 26" BHA. F/ 1369m T/ 1002m. Lubricated out due to over pull of 20 MT. F/ 1340m T/ 1303m and F/1102m T/1002." Recorded at the first (upper, 1303-1340 m) interval; the second occurrence (1002-1102 m) is the same POOH run and is noted here rather than duplicated as a separate event.

cause: Tight spot at 419 m while running in with 20" casing; set down 6 MT.
remedy: Engaged FAC tool and lubricated through the obstruction at 419 m.
free_text: "Had tight spot at 419m set down 6 MT, Engaged FAC tool and lubricated through obstruction at 419m."

cause: Tight spot F/923 m T/937 m while running in with 20" casing; set off 7-10 MT.
remedy: Washed through the tight spot.
free_text: "Tight spot F/923m T/937m, set off 7 - 10 MT and washed through."

cause: Casing tong could not make up 20" casing joints properly; investigation found a fault in the load sensor and in the tong's software.
remedy: Laid out two joints with over-torqued threads and replaced them with joints from the deck.
free_text: "Started investigating problems with casing tong load sensor." ... "Unable to make up CSG properly, investigated CSG tong, found fault in load censor and in software. Laid out two jnt w/ overtorqued threads, Replaced same w/ jnts from deck." Depth = 1045 m, the last RIH depth reached before the fault was found.

cause: Met an obstruction at 1083 m while running in with 20" casing; worked casing down with up to 50 MT to 1095 m, then hit a second obstruction at 1106 m.
remedy: Washed CSG down through both obstructions (1083->1095 m, then 1106->1120 m).
free_text: "At 1083m met obstruction. Worked casing down w/ 1200 - 200 lpm and 5 - 50 MT to 1095m. Continued to wash CSG down F/1095m T/1106m. Hit obstruction at 1106m washed down from 1106m to 1120m." Treated as one episode; interval 1083-1120 m recorded to capture both obstructions.

cause: Difficulty landing the 18 3/4" subsea wellhead: could not get it vertical without risking thread damage.
remedy: Broke out and inspected threads, then positioned it vertical and made it up the following day (07-14).
free_text: "Picked up 18 3/4" Subsea well head, attempted to make up same, had problems getting 18 3/4" Subsea well head vertical without the possibility of damaging the threads." Surface handling issue, no well depth applicable; kept as a borderline, low-confidence entry (resolved smoothly next day, no NPT hours stated).

cause: Attempting to land the tie-back connector (TBC), it was pushed aside by current just above the VX seal ring, and the VX ring came off the wellhead.
remedy: ROV was brought to surface to collect a new VX ring, which was installed on the wellhead before the landing attempt could proceed.
free_text: "Attempted to land TBC, when TBC was pushed aside due to current, VX ring came off. ROV came to surface and picked up new VX ring. Installed the new VX ring on wellhead." Subsea equipment incident, no well MD applicable.

cause: Hydraulic hose burst on the iron roughneck rollers while starting to pull out of hole with the test plug and jet sub.
remedy: Repaired hydraulic hose and fitting.
free_text: "Started to pull out of hole when hydraulic hose bursted on the iron roughneck rollers." ... "Repaired hydraulic hose and fitting." Depth = 142 m, the last stated RIH depth before the pressure test/POOH attempt.

cause: AFT PRS (pipe racking system) malfunctioned; investigation found a burst hose in the dragchain.
remedy: Repaired the hose; tested AFT PRS afterward (found tight but otherwise ok); decided to use the FWD PRS instead to continue RIH with the WBRT/nominal seat protector.
free_text: "Malfunction on AFT PRS. investigated situation, found bursted hose in dragchain ... Decided to use FWD PRS to continue RIH." Depth = 141 m, matching the nominal seat protector setting depth (141.3 m) stated a few lines later in the same operation.

cause: Repeated failed attempts ("nogo") to install the radioactive (RA) source into the ADN sub; suspected thread damage on the RA source.
remedy: Decided to change to the backup ADN and RA source; ultimately installed successfully by transferring the source directly from the installation carrier into the ADN (bypassing the adapter).
free_text: "Attempted to install RA source in ADN - nogo. Made several attempts ... nogo ... Discussed situation, suspected thread damage on RA source. Decided to change to backup ADN and RA source ... Installed RA source succesfully." Surface tool-handling issue, no well MD applicable.

cause: Problems with mud pumps #1 and #3 when bringing up rate: leakage observed on mudpump #1, liner spray on mudpump #3 not working.
remedy: Repaired both mudpumps.
free_text: "Encountered problems with mudpumps #1 and #3 when bringing up the rate. Leakage observed on mudpump #1. Liner spray on mudpump #3 not working. Repaired mudpumps." Depth = 1100 m, the RIH depth reached immediately before this line.

cause: Attempted to perform a choke drill; rig choke sensors were not reading pressures.
remedy: Investigated and found a faulty I/O module and sensor; repaired before performing the choke drill.
free_text: "Attempted to Perform choke drill. Rig choke sensors not reading pressures. Investigated sensor fault. Found faulty I/O module and sensor." ... "Performed choke drill." Depth = 1319 m, the nearest stated depth in the surrounding narrative (washing down to 1319 m).

cause: Cuttings conveyer belt overloaded and was shut down by its safety switch while drilling toward 1431 m; had to stop pumping because the belt had stopped.
remedy: Worked to clean and re-start the cuttings conveyer belt.
free_text: "Had overload of cuttings conveyer belt which was shut down by safety switch. Had to stop pumping because the cuttings conveyer belt had stopped. Worked to clean and re-start cuttings conveyer belt." Depth = 1431 m, the day's end depth (drilling was in progress toward this depth when the belt tripped).

cause: Had to stop drilling at 1436 m due to prevailing problems with the cuttings conveyer belt; not able to restart it.
remedy: Opened the forward shute, manually cleared cuttings into skips and cleaned the deck; resumed drilling at restricted ROP (30 m/hr) to test conveyer capacity.
free_text: "Had to stop drilling due to prevailing problems with cuttings conveyer belt. Not able to restart belt." ... "Restricted ROP to 30 m/hrs to check capacity of cuttings transport on conveyer belt." First of two distinct conveyer-belt escalations in this report (see next entry for the later, more severe stoppage).

cause: Cuttings conveyer belt on the main deck stopped moving completely, packed with cuttings; attempts to unplug it failed.
remedy: Decided to pull the BHA into the casing shoe (1546->1467 m) while making repairs and modifications to the conveyer belt system (cut/fitted a drainage hatch, prepared an IBC under the drain, fitted a flushing bracket, narrowed the discharge chute orifice).
free_text: "Cuttings conveyer belt on main deck stopped moving/packed with cuttings. Attempted to unplug/clean conveyer belt - nogo. Decided to pull into casing shoe while making repairs and modifications to the conveyer belt system." More severe than the 1436 m stoppage earlier in the same report -- this one forced a full trip and rig repairs, not just a restricted-ROP workaround.

cause: Tight hole while pulling out of hole with the 17 1/2" drilling BHA, from 1546 m to 1467 m.
remedy: Worked through with approx 30 MT overpull.
free_text: "POOH with 17 1/2" drilling BHA from 1546 m to 1467 m MD. Tight hole took approx 30 MT overpull." Canonical tight-hole/overpull pattern; this is the event that both the round-1 and round-2 extraction passes missed (see VOLVE_EVAL_NOTES.md).

cause: Static losses of approx 100 l/hr observed while lining up well on trip tank and changing from PS-30 to manual slips.
free_text: "Lined up well on triptank. Changed from PS-30 to manual slips. Static losses approx 100 l/hrs." No explicit depth on this line; used the last stated depth in the report (1354 m, reached POOH 'while pumping from 1467 m to 1354 m MD inside casing' immediately before this line) rather than the day-header depth (1546 m). A second, smaller static-loss reading later in the same report ("Static losses 30 l/hrs", during conveyer-belt repairs) is treated as a continuation/decline of this same background condition, not a separate event.
